name: WGPU Frame Telemetry

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

primaryTarget: gpui_wgpu rayx_diagnostics with apps/test_suite wide DataTable headed WebGPU
hypothesisMarkdown:
# Hypothesis

Feature-gated renderer-owned telemetry can expose the actual WGPU work generated by each gpux frame—scene primitive counts, scene batches, instance and gradient bytes written, queue buffer/texture writes, bind groups created, render passes, atlas uploads, and instance-buffer restarts—without changing release behavior when `rayx_diagnostics` is disabled. Publishing only the latest bounded numeric snapshot to the existing Test Suite diagnostic bridge will make subsequent renderer hypotheses measurable and will reveal whether current wide-table frames pay the expected per-batch packing/binding costs.
measurementPlanMarkdown:
# Measurement plan

1. Add one diagnostics-only numeric frame snapshot owned by `gpui_wgpu`; compile it out without `rayx_diagnostics`.
2. Increment counters at existing renderer and atlas operations only; do not alter operation order, allocation ownership, batching, shaders, or scene semantics.
3. Publish the latest snapshot through the existing `gpui_web` diagnostics boundary without content samples or unbounded history.
4. Extend the existing wide DataTable Test Suite benchmark to assert WebGPU telemetry is present, internally consistent, and bounded at DPR1 and DPR2.
5. Run focused Rust tests, source guard, diagnostics-off compilation, diagnostics-on compilation, and the headed WebGPU benchmark. Compare the benchmark medians with a fresh serialized checkpoint run; reject if the gated-off path changes or the diagnostic path breaks correctness.
expectedOutcomeMarkdown:
# Expected outcome

The wide-table workload reports stable nonzero primitive, batch, write, bind-group, and render-pass counts for its last rendered frame; atlas uploads are zero after warmup unless new glyphs/images are introduced. Production builds contain no telemetry state or publication path when `rayx_diagnostics` is disabled. All existing DPR1/DPR2 correctness gates remain green, and the numbers are sufficient to choose one renderer optimization mechanism for experiment 3.

playwright: apps/test_suite wide DataTable headed WebGPU passed 2/2 at DPR1 and DPR2 with one worker.
Both projects asserted telemetry schema, primitive and batch counts, byte/write consistency, bounded bind groups, render passes, atlas upload consistency, and one submission.

reportMarkdown:
# WGPU frame telemetry report

The diagnostics-only latest-frame snapshot is implemented in `gpui_wgpu`, published by `gpui_web`, and asserted by the existing wide DataTable Test Suite benchmark. The feature-off native and WASM builds compile without telemetry state or publication code.

The headed WebGPU benchmark passed at DPR1 and DPR2. Its final warm frame contained 1,737 primitives at DPR1 and 1,735 at DPR2, merged into nine scene batches. Each frame used 12 queue buffer writes, 10 transient bind groups, two render passes, one submission, and no instance-buffer restart. The instance payload was 240,096 bytes at DPR1 and 239,840 bytes at DPR2. Atlas uploads were zero after warmup.

Against the immediately preceding serialized baseline, median acknowledged throughput was 5.21% higher at DPR1 and 2.01% higher at DPR2. Paced p95 catch-up was 0.29% lower at DPR1 and 2.76% higher at DPR2. These variations are within ordinary browser-run noise and are not attributed to the telemetry change; all correctness gates retained zero terminal error.

Validation passed for diagnostics-off and diagnostics-on `gpui_wgpu` checks, diagnostics-off and diagnostics-on `gpui_web` WASM checks, gpui_wgpu Clippy with warnings denied, nested gpux formatting, diff checks, and the focused headed WebGPU benchmark. The repository root formatting command hit Windows path-length error 206. The broader gpui_wgpu unit run exposed the pre-existing `transformed_quad_uses_analytic_coverage` string assertion and later stalled in GPU-backed tests; the focused renderer assertion was captured and is outside this experiment's diff.
decisionMarkdown:
# Decision

Accept the telemetry mechanism. It preserves release behavior through compile-time feature gating and provides enough bounded renderer evidence to choose the next atomic mechanism.

Experiment 3 should prepack ordinary primitive families once per frame and reuse family-owned bindings across their batch ranges. The telemetry shows nine batches currently cause nine instance writes plus nine transient batch bind groups, in addition to the frame's three global writes and one post-process bind group. The next experiment must preserve the WebGPU storage-buffer ABI, WebGL2 packed-texture ABI, scene ordering, visual/screen effect interruptions, and overflow behavior.
